title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The war has now reached the UAE's own bypass feeders: an AD Ports-owned container ship on the Khor Fakkan–Fujairah–Karachi service was sunk this week and a second was damaged. Missile attacks have also shut Riyadh airport, so both the sea gateway on the east coast and the air link into Saudi Arabia are under pressure.

stories.headline: AD Ports-owned feeder sunk on a UAE east-coast service
body: The 2,824 TEU GFS Pride was hit by a missile off Oman on Tuesday, caught fire and sank. It ran the Khor Fakkan–Fujairah–Karachi service. Its sister ship GFS Giselle (Fujairah–Khor Fakkan–Nhava Sheva) was damaged but reached anchorage. All crew are safe. Both were due in Khor Fakkan today.
Abu Dhabi's AD Ports owns 81% of operator Global Feeder Shipping. It is the second ship sunk since the war began in February. The IMO counts 113 incidents and 24 seafarers killed.
stories.soWhat: The east-coast bypass is no longer out of range. Expect gaps on UAE–Pakistan and UAE–India feeder sailings and higher cover costs on these lanes.

stories.headline: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move Far East service to Khor Fakkan as congestion builds
body: The Gemini partners relaunch their Far East–Middle East loop (FM1/AGX) on 17 October, with Khor Fakkan replacing Jebel Ali. Kuehne+Nagel expects significant pressure at Khor Fakkan and Fujairah in the coming weeks. Maersk reports berth shortages, full yards and long truck waits, and is moving some boxes to an inland depot at Sajja.
Forwarders say the best-funded players have taken most of the trucking capacity. A DP World official puts overland moves at four to five times the cost of sailing through Hormuz.
stories.soWhat: Trucks from the east coast are now the bottleneck. Whoever holds road capacity into Dubai can charge for it.

stories.headline: Riyadh airport suspended after missile strikes; Dammam also hit
body: King Khalid International Airport stopped operations after missile attacks on its infrastructure, and extended the suspension after another strike on Sunday. Hundreds of flights were cancelled. Saudi aviation authorities said Dammam airport was also targeted on 11 October. Europe's safety regulator told airlines to avoid airspace around Riyadh and Dammam.
stories.soWhat: Air express into Saudi Arabia's two main cities is unreliable. Road from the UAE becomes the main way to serve KSA customers.

stories.headline: dnata spends Dh175m on new ramp equipment at Dubai's airports
body: dnata has committed Dh175 million this year to more than 340 new ground-handling assets in the UAE. It runs about 2,800 motorised units at DXB and DWC, and handled 3.2 million tonnes of cargo last financial year.
stories.soWhat: Dubai's airports are adding handling capacity while Saudi hubs are disrupted, which supports DXB/DWC as the region's air gateway.

stories.headline: Al Sharqi opens AED 70m cold-chain hub with its own rail terminal
body: Al Sharqi Shipping opened a multi-temperature hub at Dubai Industrial City: 280,000 sq ft of storage, 22,000 pallet tonnes from ambient to −18°C, 38 loading lanes and up to 178 trucks a day. An Etihad Rail freight terminal sits on site. It targets food, FMCG, retail, HoReCa and quick commerce.
stories.soWhat: A local rival now offers cold storage linked to rail from the east-coast ports, exactly where demand is moving.

competitors.name: JD.com
competitors.headline: JD's property arm plans a 2.5m sq ft fulfilment hub in Dubai
body: Gargash Prime and JINGDONG Property, JD.com's infrastructure arm, signed an MoU on 13 October for a joint venture to build a regional distribution and fulfilment hub of about 2.5 million sq ft in Dubai. JD.com Middle East's CEO said the aim is more efficient regional supply chains. No cost or opening date was given.
competitors.soWhat: JD is building scale for Chinese sellers into the Gulf. Its fulfilment could pull last-mile and cross-border volume away from us unless we partner early.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: DHL launches six air cold-chain corridors, with the Middle East next
body: DHL Global Forwarding opened six temperature-controlled air corridors linking Europe and the US with Shanghai, Singapore, Tokyo and Seoul, using 777 freighters with three separate temperature zones. It says Middle East routes will follow.
competitors.soWhat: Coming after FedEx's Dubai pharma certification last week, healthcare is the segment rivals are racing for. We have a short window before DHL's Gulf corridors land.

competitors.name: Rhenus
competitors.headline: Rhenus opens aid logistics office in Dubai Humanitarian
body: Rhenus opened an emergency aid and relief office in the Dubai Humanitarian free zone on 14 October. It will move medical products, pharmaceuticals, food aid and shelter materials by air, sea and road. The zone has about 80 members, including UN bodies and NGOs.
competitors.soWhat: Aid flows across a region at war are a growing, time-critical business, and a European forwarder has just set up next to the buyers.

opportunities.title: Road express into Saudi Arabia
opportunities.text: With Riyadh airport shut and Dammam targeted, KSA customers need a dependable road option from the UAE.

opportunities.title: East-coast trucking capacity
opportunities.text: Khor Fakkan and Fujairah are congested and trucks are scarce. Guaranteed road legs into Dubai have real value.

opportunities.title: India and Pakistan shippers losing feeder sailings
opportunities.text: The sunk and damaged ships served Karachi and Nhava Sheva. Some of that cargo will need air or sea-air options.

opportunities.title: Cold chain before DHL arrives
opportunities.text: DHL says Middle East cold-chain corridors are next and Al Sharqi has just opened a −18°C hub. Healthcare and food shippers are choosing partners now.

opportunities.title: Humanitarian logistics
opportunities.text: Dubai Humanitarian has about 80 members, including UN bodies and NGOs, shipping medical and relief goods across the region.

watchouts.title: Attacks on east-coast feeders
watchouts.text: Ships serving Khor Fakkan and Fujairah are now being hit, not only ships inside the Gulf.

watchouts.title: Khor Fakkan congestion from 17 October
watchouts.text: The Gemini loop adds volume to a port that already has full yards and long truck queues.

watchouts.title: Saudi air network
watchouts.text: Riyadh is suspended and Dammam was targeted. Air-reliant KSA service promises are at risk.

watchouts.title: Fuel costs into November
watchouts.text: Brent is near $105 and war-risk cover on tankers is 6–10% of hull value. Plan for diesel staying high.

watchouts.title: Rivals building in Dubai
watchouts.text: JD is planning a 2.5m sq ft hub and Al Sharqi has opened a rail-linked cold store.

moves.title: Switch KSA express to road while Riyadh is shut
moves.text: Re-plan UAE–Riyadh and UAE–Dammam shipments by road, tell key accounts the new transit times, and price it as a service option.

moves.title: Book east-coast trucks before 17 October
moves.text: Secure road capacity from Khor Fakkan and Fujairah before the Gemini loop adds volume, and quote it as a bundled bridge price.

moves.title: Call India and Pakistan sea shippers today
moves.text: List customers on Karachi and Nhava Sheva feeder lanes and offer air or sea-air alternatives with a firm price.

moves.title: Prepare a November fuel surcharge scenario
moves.text: Model domestic and road surcharges with Brent around $105 so tables can move as soon as November pump prices are out.

moves.title: Pitch cold chain to healthcare and food shippers
moves.text: Target pharma and F&B accounts before DHL's Middle East corridors and Al Sharqi's new hub win them.

moves.title: Approach Gargash Prime and JD about last mile
moves.text: Offer delivery and cross-border services to the new Dubai fulfilment hub before JD builds its own network.
